title: SRE Ops Sprint Bridgeboard — Apr 11–17, 2027
content:
Context:
This note is the sprint-bridging update for the SRE team covering operational events, SLO posture, and handoff items for the week of Apr 11–17, 2027. Intended audience: on-call, platform owners, infra leads, and product stakeholders.

Quick TL;DR:
- Three notable incidents (one sev2, two sev3) — all recovered with partial mitigations and follow-ups planned.
- Overall token-generation SLO met at 99.7% (30-day rolling) but tail latency regressed ~120ms at p99 on Apr 13 during sustained batch jobs.
- Runbook gaps identified for model-variant fallback; update planned before next canary.
- On-call handoff checklist expanded — see "Handoff notes" below.

Incidents (brief):
1) INC-2345 — "GRPC pool exhaustion during bulk-embed jobs" (Apr 13, sev2):
   - Symptoms: elevated request queueing and client timeouts for embedding endpoints for ~48 minutes.
   - Root cause (initial): sudden increase in long-running embed requests from a single partner job that did not respect the batching window; upstream retries amplified pressure.
   - Mitigation: deployed emergency rate-limit on partner token + scaled embed worker pool by 2x.
   - Follow-ups: SRE-1123 (rate-limit policy enforcement + traffic-contract with partner), owner: Priya, due: 2027-04-22.

2) INC-2378 — "Fallback chain misconfiguration" (Apr 15, sev3):
   - Symptoms: Canary fallback to quantized model failed due to mismatched KV-cache format causing 502s for ~12 minutes.
   - Mitigation: rolled back canary. Quick patch created in runtime PR #789.
   - Follow-ups: add preflight KV-format check in rollout pipeline, update rollout runbook. Owner: Miguel, due: 2027-04-20.

3) INC-2391 — "Control-plane auth flakiness" (Apr 16, sev3):
   - Symptoms: sporadic 401s for internal admin operations (not customer-facing), ~4 incidents over 3 hours.
   - Mitigation: rotated short-lived token issuer and tightened caching TTL.
   - Follow-ups: deeper auth library audit (SRE ticket), owner: Sophie, due: 2027-04-29.

SLO snapshot (30-day rolling):
- Text-generation availability SLO (>= 99.5): 99.7% — PASS but margin tightened.
- Embeddings availability SLO (>= 99.6): 99.65% — PASS.
- Request p99 latency (generation): baseline 220ms; observed spike to 340ms on Apr 13 during incident window.

Operational observations:
- Autoscaling: observed slow scale-up (~60s) when burst of long-lived embed requests hit the pool; suggests need for faster warm cold start or pre-warming for known partners.
- Batching effectiveness: batch sizes drift when partner jobs send single-token high-frequency requests; quality of batching suffers.
- Observability: synthetic canary checks caught the KV fallback mismatch (good), but the canary alert to SRE was routed to a private channel and missed by morning shift — fix alert ownership.

Handoff notes (outgoing -> incoming):
- Outgoing oncall: Ravi Menon (ends 2027-04-17 09:00 UTC).
- Incoming oncall: Priya Desai (starts 2027-04-17 09:00 UTC).
- Critical things to watch: partner embed queue length, rollout pipeline runs (especially kv-cache-aware canaries), autoscale-signal delay metric (metric name: runtime.autoscale.delay_ms).
- Pending runbook edits: fallback-runbook.md (section: KV cache compatibility), embed-rate-limits.md (add partner policy).
- Pager escalations: for any repeating 5xx spikes > 10m escalate to SRE lead and infra-ops.

Action items (concise):
- Priya: Draft partner traffic contract + automated rate-limit enforcement (JIRA SRE-1123), due 2027-04-22.
- Miguel: Add KV-format preflight to rollout pipeline + unit tests (PR: #789 merged as patch but needs automated test), due 2027-04-20.
- Sophie: Auth library audit + remediation plan, due 2027-04-29.
- Evan: Run staggered canary exercise next Friday (2027-04-23) to validate fallback paths under load.

Runbook/Playbook changes needed:
- Add a quick validation step to the model-variant rollout runbook that compares KV cache header versions before switching traffic.
- Add a short checklist for embedding partner onboarding (min batch sizes, retry behavior, expected QPS).
- Update escalation matrix to include exact Slack channel and on-call rotation owner for canary alerts.

Metrics appendix (quick numbers):
- Average requests/min (gen): 3,200
- Average requests/min (embed): 420
- p95 latency (gen): 135ms
- p99 latency (gen): 340ms (spike on Apr 13)
- Error rate (5xx) weekly average: 0.22%

Run-of-week notes / informal: 
- "Notes to self": need to carve out 2 hours in next sprint to do a canary blackout drill.
- Saw a pattern where partner job retries were exponential and clobbered the batching window — consider a partner SDK snippet / client-side guidance.
- Ops hack: temporary mitigation for embed storm was to set k8s pod terminationGracePeriod to 15s to speed replacement — not ideal long-term.

Open questions / discussion points for next sync:
- Do we enforce stricter partner SLAs around batching and retries or implement automatic throttles?
- Should we spin up a smaller dedicated embed pool for high-volume partners to isolate impact?
- Can we get a product commitment to sponsor the runbook time?

Next week's focus:
- Complete listed follow-ups (SRE-1123, rollout pipeline checks, auth audit).
- Schedule and run the canary exercise (Evan lead).
- Start design for dedicated embed isolation (mini-pool proposal).

If you pick this up as incoming on-call, first actions:
1) Check synthetic canary dashboard (dash: SRE / Canary-Global).
2) Confirm alert routing — send a quick readout in #sre-ops if alerts reroute.
3) Review the three follow-up tickets and confirm owners/ETA.

End of bridgeboard.
